summary.en-US: On macOS, a two-finger swipe right on a tab with no previous page closes it and returns to the tab that opened it. Works with container and non-container tabs.

description.en-US:
Swiping right with two fingers on a Mac trackpad normally goes back a page. When a tab has no previous page (for example, a link you opened in a new tab), this add-on makes that swipe close the tab and switch to the tab that opened it.

- Works with Firefox Multi-Account Containers and with tabs that Facebook Container or Google Container reopen in another container.
- If the tab that opened it is gone, it goes to the next tab up the chain.
- When the tab has a previous page, the browser goes back as usual.
- Parent links survive browser restarts.

Requires a trackpad on macOS. Doesn't work on about: pages, addons.mozilla.org or other extensions' pages, where Firefox doesn't let add-ons run.

version.approval_notes:
No build step and no minified code: the uploaded files are the source (https://github.com/wrwrc/swipe-back-to-parent-tab).

Permissions:
- <all_urls>: only for the content script, which watches horizontal trackpad scroll (wheel) events to recognise the swipe gesture.
- sessions: stores each tab's parent link as a session tab value so it survives restarts.
- storage: settings, plus a capped list of closed tabs' parents.

No network requests are made and no data leaves the device.

To test on macOS: open a link in a new tab, then swipe right with two fingers on the trackpad. The tab closes and its parent tab is selected.
